articles.title: Bank of America hit with $1.2 billion penalty over money laundering allegations
WTF Was Trump’s New Press Secretary Doing in China?
articles.description: It’s not clear if new White House press secretary Katie Zacharia ever actually worked as an attorney—but it is becoming increasingly clear that she was connected to the Chinese government in the past. Speaking alongside Donald Trump Tuesday, Zacharia informed reporters inquiring about her self-purported legal qualifications that she passed the bar exam when she “moved to China.” Popular Info’s Judd Legum found that, after analyzing state bar association databases from all 50 states and Washington, Zacharia never actually passed the qualifying legal exam anywhere in the country. But she couldn’t have passed the Chinese equivalent of the bar exam, either, as it’s actually forbidden for foreigners to do so. Zacharia’s LinkedIn work history places her at Zhong Lun, an elite Chinese multinational law firm, between 2011 and 2013. She worked at the Beijing-based firm as an associate on the international practice team, months after she obtained her J.D. from Pepperdine Caruso Law. Zacharia’s LinkedIn also notes that she spoke Chinese at an “elementary proficiency.” Like many major Chinese businesses, Zhong Lung operates in an environment in which it can be influenced by the regional government. Since it was founded in 1993, the firm has provided legal services to numerous Chinese government agencies and state-owned enterprises. Some of those entities include China’s Ministry of Justice, People’s Bank of China, the Ministry of Commerce, Ministry of Finance, Ministry of Natural Resources, Ministry of Ecology and Environment, and other regulatory bodies, according to the firm’s webpage. Within that same time period, Zacharia also worked as the manager of fundraising and communications at Compassion for Migrant Children, a Beijing-based nonprofit that provided education and material support to rural migrant workers. The group also noted in an archived profile that it “engage[d] the Chinese government and local educational officials for greater and longer lasting impact.”

articles.title: White House enraged after Kaitlan Collins shares embarrassing clip of Trump's empty seats
articles.description: For the second time in three days, the White House is blaming the press for the empty seats at a Trump rally. The White House’s Rapid Response 47 account hit back at CNN’s Kaitlan Collins after she aired footage of bare upper sections at President Donald Trump’s Monday night rally in Youngstown, Ohio. “The only one humiliated here is @kaitlancollins. These ‘vacant seats’ had an obstructed view due to the gigantic press risers directly in front of them. Just more Fake News bulls---,” the account posted on X. The account made nearly the same claim days earlier. After New York Times reporter Shawn McCreesh posted video of whole empty sections at Trump’s rally in Clarksville, Tennessee on Saturday, Rapid Response said those seats were “purposely left empty” because anyone sitting in them would have had their view blocked by “gigantic press risers,” the Irish Star reported. The Youngstown explanation doesn’t account for local reporting. Station WFMJ found that tarps covered roughly a quarter of the Covelli Centre’s seating, and that the crowd never filled more than about two-thirds of the seats left open. The Tribune Chronicle estimated 2,500 to 3,000 people attended, compared with roughly 7,000 at Trump’s 2017 rally in the same arena. The paper also reported that about half the permanent seats were closed off before the event began. Collins had allowed on “The Source” that it was hard to know how much to read into the turnout. She noted that Trump is the one who has been claiming his events need big overflow rooms. The press riser defense is the latest in a string of explanations. Last week, Trump insisted that supporters seated up high routinely “migrate down to the Main Floor” and declared that he never has empty seats. Collins has been a frequent target. Trump mocked her looks at the White House Correspondents’ Dinner in July and told her to “smile.” The fight over the crowd comes as Republicans scramble to hold Ohio. A CNN poll released last week showed Democrat Sherrod Brown leading Republican Sen. Jon Husted 49 percent to 43 percent among likely voters.
